@context.shell.bar.area.app: App bar chip and link: the app area for online apps (/app). Keep it short.

shell.engines.button.title: Engines: schematics, networks, motion, queues, schedule, requirements, risk, live data, circuits, boards, systems and PLC
shell.engines.what: Run one of the shared engines on a model you paste or one of its worked examples. Everything runs in this page; nothing is sent anywhere. Problems also appear in the Problems panel.
shell.engines.schematic.name: Schematics and connectivity
shell.engines.schematic.summary: Symbols, pins, nets, wire and terminal numbers, cross-references, plans, bill of materials and twelve rule checks.
shell.engines.network.name: Pipe networks and power systems
shell.engines.network.summary: Pipe network flows and pressures, power load flow, short circuit, protection curves.
shell.engines.motion.name: Motion and robots
shell.engines.motion.summary: Robot chains, forward and inverse kinematics, joint torques, trajectories, URDF in and out; closed planar loops (four-bar, slider-crank, parallel robots) with Grashof class and velocity ratios.
shell.engines.des.name: Queues and flow simulation
shell.engines.des.summary: Discrete-event simulation of queues, servers, conveyors and shifts, with replications.
shell.engines.schedule.name: Schedule and cost
shell.engines.schedule.summary: Critical path with lags and calendars, resources, cost curve and earned value.
shell.engines.trace.name: Requirements and traceability
shell.engines.trace.summary: Requirements linked to elements and tests, coverage matrix, impact, ReqIF in and out.
shell.engines.risk.name: Risk and reliability
shell.engines.risk.summary: Fault trees, reliability blocks, FMEA, Weibull fits, Markov models.
shell.engines.live.name: Live data
shell.engines.live.summary: Modbus, MQTT and BACnet message codecs and the tag store with markers (read-only).
shell.engines.em.name: Circuits and fields
shell.engines.em.summary: A circuit solver for a netlist: operating point, sweep, AC and transient.
shell.engines.pcb.name: Boards
shell.engines.pcb.summary: Place and route a board from a netlist, check the design rules, write Gerber and IPC-2581.
shell.engines.sys.name: Systems (lumped models)
shell.engines.sys.summary: Acausal models across electrical, thermal, hydraulic and mechanical domains; a Modelica subset reader.
shell.engines.plc.name: Controls (PLC)
shell.engines.plc.summary: IEC 61131-3 structured text: check it, scan it, watch the variables.

shell.fit.offer: Switch to a tighter layout? Tools go in one scrolling row, the ribbon folds to its tab names, and the buttons lose their labels if that is still not enough. You can change it back in Settings.
shell.fit.more.lead: Three ways to give the drawing more room:
shell.fit.more.1: Settings › Toolbar rows: wrap to fit, two rows, or one row that scrolls sideways.
shell.fit.more.2: Settings › Toolbar buttons: icons and labels, icons only or labels only. A ribbon folds to its tab names from its right-click menu.
shell.fit.more.3: Full screen (F11, or the corner button in the top bar) hides the browser's own bars and gives the window back its height. Zooming the page out (Ctrl and minus) also helps.
shell.fit.more.4: Chose Don't ask again by mistake? Open the command palette and run "Check the layout fit", or clear this site's data for the key cc-fit.
shell.fit.never.said: Okay, no more layout questions. Settings still has every layout choice.
shell.fit.done: Layout tightened: the toolbars now take {n}% of the window's height. Change it any time in Settings.
shell.fit.nothing: The layout was already as tight as it goes. Try full screen (F11) or zooming the page out.
shell.fit.fine: The toolbars leave the drawing plenty of room in this window.
